 Judgment

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.200,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.10.2023 at about 8.00am.

2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 09.10.2023 at about 8.00am the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HY- 5657 from Kodigehalli to Hoodi Main Road near SJR Phase 2 layout, a TATA Ace Mega XL bearing No.KA- 53-D-1018 which was parked near Nandini Milk Parlour for unloading the goods without following any safety measures,
all of a sudden the driver of the said vehicle without showing any hand signal or any gestures, he getting out of the vehicle has opened the right side of the vehicle's door i.e., the Driver's side Door.
Due to forceful opening of the door which hit the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down on the ground and sustained injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, near ITPL Road,
Shantinekethan, provided first aid and MLC was done and thereafter referred to a Surgeon
, the surgeon who addressed the petitioner said that it was worse the bone of Index Finger is broken and he had to undergo an anaesthetic surgery.
Thereafter the petitioner was admitted at Manipla Hospital, underwent surgery and discharged on 10.10.2023 with advice to take rest.
So far he has spent huge amount towards medical, hospital charges, medicines, attendant charges, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental expenses.
Due to the said accidental injuries, he could not do his normal work as previous and could not attend the office and lost salary.

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, working as an Advocate and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month and was contributing his entire income for welfare and maintenance of his family.

The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent by the driver of the parked Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-1018 and KR Puram Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.347/2023 p/u/Secs.283 &
338 of IPC and 134 (a & b), 187, 146, 196, 56, 192 of MV Act.
The respondents being the RC owner and the Driver of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant compensation as prayed in the petition.
4. In response to the service of summons, the respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed exparte.
4A. The respondent No.2 has denied the entire petition averments.
Further denied the manner of accident, injuries suffered by the petitioner.
He further denied the medical expenses incurred by him.
The accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
He dashed himself to the lorry in a rash and negligent manner and contributing to the alleged accident.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Therefore,
prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.
5. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 09-10-2023 at 8:00am due to negligent parking of Goods vehicle Reg.No.KA-53-D-1018 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
Issue No.2: Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum ?
Form whom?
Issue No.3:- What order or Award?
6. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Twenty-Four documents as Exs.P1 to P24.
The respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
7. The Court has heard the arguments canvassed by both sides counsel.

8. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above points are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the foregoing #REASONS#

9. Issue No.1:-
In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Nine documents as Exs.P1 to P24.
The respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
10. The chief examination of the PW.1 is nothing but a repetition of plaint averments.
The PW.1 has been subjected to cross examination.
During the cross examination of PW.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
He further denied other material suggestions of the counsel in the cross examination.
11. It is the specific defense of the driver that the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
12. The petitioner has totally relied on the police documents to establish the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle's driver.
It is no doubt the police have submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending Goods vehicle after thorough investigation.

The spot sketch appended to the spot mahazar indicates that the accident was occurred at SJR Layout, near Phase - II, infront of Nandini Milk Parlour the offending vehicle was parked without any indication and the driver of the said vehicle suddenly opened his side door to jump down from the vehicle, at that time the petitioner was coming in the same way and hit the door to the petitioner and caused the accident.
The accident spot is at the left side of the Kodigehalli Main Road towards Hoodi.
It is undisputed fact that the offending vehicle was parked on the left side of the Kodigehalli Main Road towards Hoodi.
The accident spot clearly depicts that the petitioner has proceeding from Kodigehalli Main Road towards Hoodi without observing parked vehicle.
In the same time, the driver of the Goods vehicle has also taken minimal care of coming vehicles while open the driver's Door to get down.
The petitioner has produce the Motor Vehicle Inspection report at Ex.P.12 stating that the Goods vehicle got damaged to its front right side door.

On careful perusal of the entire material on record,
it is worth to note herein that the offending vehicle was parked in the road without any parking lights being switched on and the driver of the offending vehicle used to open his door without observing the oncoming vehicles.
The rider or driver of coming vehicles cannot be expected the acts of driver of stationed vehicle.
Hence, I decline to hold contributory negligence as contemplated or defense setout in the cross examination by the respondent Counsel.
In support of these findings I would like rely on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reported in 12024 SCC OnLine SC 2584.
So, it is appears to the Court that the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the respondent No.1 or driver of the offending vehicle.
So, I hold issue No.1 in affirmative.
13. Issue No.2: the claimant has produced Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.10.
It shows that the claimant has sustained Total amputation of left Index finger with fracture tip of terminal phalanx and nail avulsion which is grievous in nature.

Though the claimant is able to prove that he has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident but he has failed to prove that he had sustained permanent disability due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Considering the contents of wound certificate and nature of injury sustained in the accident, it can be 1 Sushma VS Nitin Ganapathi Rangole and others.

sentences.text: The petitioner has also produced final bill at Ex.P.16 for Rs.99,885/- of Manipal Hospital and
The petitioner has produced the out patient bills and vehicle repair invoice for Rs.17,406/-.
The discharge summary shows that the petitioner has taken treatment at Manipal Hospital from 09.10.2023 to 10.10.2023 for 2 days.
The petitioner has produced the out patient bills and vehicle repair invoice.

Therefore, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident, nature of treatment taken by him, the period in which he has taken treatment as out- patient and also amount spent towards treatment,
repair of the motor vehicle, I am of the firm opinion that awarding a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- as Global compensation under only one conventional head meets the ends of justice.

The certified copy of the order sheet pertaining criminal case produced by the petitioner is clearly reflects that the respondent No.1 has got released the offending vehicle to his interim custody by claiming he is the owner of the vehicle.
So, in view of, I answer issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part against the respondent No.1.

The respondent No.1 is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.3,00,000/-
(Rupees Three Lakhs only) together interest @ 6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.
The Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the said amount within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
On deposit of compensation, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw entire amount with interest as awarded amount is meager one.
The office is directed to release the entire amount to petitioner or PW.1 with interest through e- payment.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.

The advocate fee of Rs.1,000/-
 fixed.
Draw the award accordingly.
